title: Lee Kang-cheol vows to deliver after record 3.4 billion won re-signing
text:
Lee Kang-cheol vows to deliver after record 3.4 billion won re-signing - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 3일(화) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Lee Kang-cheol vows to deliver after record 3.4 billion won re-signing 
 입력 2026.11.03. 17:30 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 "There is nowhere to run now that they re-signed me."
 KT Wiz manager Lee Kang-cheol signed a three-year aggregates 3.4 billion won contract on Oct. 19 last month, extending his tenure through 2029. This exceeds the 3-year 3 billion won deal for LG Twins manager Youm Kyoung-youb, making it the highest-paid managerial contract in KBO League history. Including his milestone of 600 career wins and this season's regular-season championship, he led KT to the Korean Series for the first time in five years and succeeded in a mega re-signing.
 Before the Korean Series Game 1 against the Samsung Lions at Suwon KT Wiz Park on the 3rd, manager Lee Kang-cheol, whom we met, said, "It's been eight years since I came to this team, and I feel it has improved a lot. Because the players have played well, we were able to reach the Korean Series three times. Everything fell into place, and we came this far," expressing his deep feelings.
 Manager Lee Kang-cheol said the last two Korean Series (2021, 2023) were not a great burden. Raising the youngest club, which had long lingered at the bottom, to the pinnacle of the Korean Series was considered a sufficient success.
 Manager Lee Kang-cheol said, "Until now I thought, 'It's enough if I came to this team and made it this way.' It was my own mind control to make the game comfortable. As a player and when playing big games, I always tried to enter as comfortably as possible with positive thinking."
 But this year is different. It is already the third Korean Series, and with the hope of the group's second overall championship in five years, he received the highest-ever amount.
 Manager Lee Kang-cheol said, "They re-signed me this year, so I have to produce results worthy of that. I'm nervous," and added, "In the first Korean Series I had won the regular season, so I thought the fall postseason was a bonus. But it seems that won't be the case this year. The media keeps saying we're a good team, so there is nowhere to run. Unlike usual, there is a pressure that we must win this series."
 Meanwhile, KT set a starting lineup against Samsung starter Choi Won-tae of Choi Won-joon (right field), Kim Min-hyuk (left field), designated hitter Ahn Hyun-min, Sam Hilliard (center field), Kim Hyun-soo (first base), Kim Sang-su (second base), Heo Kyung-min (third base), Han Seung-taek (catcher) and Jang Jun-won (shortstop). The starting pitcher is Davis Daniel.
